Content:
Suppose we know that the triangles [MATH: ABC] and [MATH: NLM] shown below are similar such that [MATH: \triangle ABC\sim\triangle NLM.] How do we find the length of [MATH: \overline{NL}?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/64cc605ac09916a50ca8987ce707bbe6]

Content:
According to the similarity statement, [MATH: \triangle ABC\sim \triangle NLM.] Therefore,

Content:
- [MATH: \overline{AB}] corresponds to [MATH: \overline{NL},]
- [MATH: \overline{BC}] corresponds to [MATH: \overline{LM},]
- [MATH: \overline{AC}] corresponds to [MATH: \overline{NM}.]

Content:
In similar polygons, the ratio of any two corresponding sides are in proportion. Therefore, we have

Content:
[MATH: (AC)/(NM)|= (AB)/(NL); (12)/(9)|= (20)/(NL); (9)/(12)|= (NL)/(20); NL|= (20 ⋅ 9)/(12); NL|= 15.]

[MATH: m \angle L = m \angle B = 80^\circ.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
According to the similarity statement, [MATH: \triangle ABC\sim \triangle PQR.] Therefore,

  • [MATH: \overline{AB}] corresponds to [MATH: \overline{PQ},]

  • [MATH: \overline{BC}] corresponds to [MATH: \overline{QR},]

  • [MATH: \overline{AC}] corresponds to [MATH: \overline{PR}.]

In similar polygons, corresponding sides are proportional. Therefore, we have

[MATH: (AB)/(PQ)|= (AC)/(PR); (6)/(2)|= (9)/(PR); PR|= (9 ⋅ 2)/(6); PR|= 3.]

sections.normalized_html: The triangles [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle A'B'C'] are similar. The perimeter of the triangle [MATH: \triangle ABC] is [MATH: 30\, \mathrm{cm},] and [MATH: {AB}=12\, \mathrm{cm}.] If the perimeter of the triangle [MATH: \triangle A'B'C'] is [MATH: 60 \, \mathrm{cm},] determine the value of [MATH: A'B'.]

The triangles [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle A'B'C'] are similar. The perimeter of the triangle [MATH: \triangle ABC] is [MATH: 30\, \mathrm{cm},] and [MATH: {AB}=12\, \mathrm{cm}.] If the perimeter of the triangle [MATH: \triangle A'B'C'] is [MATH: 60 \, \mathrm{cm},] determine the value of [MATH: A'B'.]

[IMG: /graphics/aad4dffbc843a6cba8cf397e66664361]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
In similar polygons, the ratio of the perimeters is equal to the similarity ratio. So, the similarity ratio is

[MATH: k=\dfrac{p_{\triangle A'B'C'}}{p_{\triangle ABC}}=\dfrac{60}{30}=2.]

Notice that [MATH: \overline{AB}] is the longest side of [MATH: ABC.] So, it corresponds to the longest side [MATH: \overline{A'B'}] of [MATH: A'B'C'.] As a result, we obtain

[MATH: (A^{′}B^{′})/(AB)|= k; (A^{′}B^{′})/(AB)|= 2; (A^{′}B^{′})/(12)|= 2; A^{′}B^{′}|= 24cm.]
